issues.description: The problem specification and UML explicitly require a method named checkOrderReady() in SealSaloon to process and serve orders. The solution implementation uses a method named processOrders() (and orderMeal calls processOrders()). This name mismatch between the expected API (checkOrderReady) and the solution implementation may confuse students about the required method name and expected behavior, and could cause tests or graders that look for checkOrderReady() to fail.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the implementation and the specification consistent: either rename the solution method processOrders() to checkOrderReady(), or add a public checkOrderReady() method that delegates to processOrders(). Alternatively, update the problem statement/UML to use processOrders() instead of checkOrderReady() so the expected API name matches the implementation.

issues.description: The problem statement specifies a method named checkOrderReady(), but the solution implementation provides an equivalently behaving method named processOrders(). issues.suggestedFix: Align the names so the specification and implementation match. Either rename the solution method processOrders() to checkOrderReady(), or add a checkOrderReady() wrapper that delegates to processOrders(). Update any references (and tests) accordingly so students can directly map the required checkOrderReady() behavior to the code.
